newsitem.title: DENMARK: Nervous Danish bonds follow foreign markets down.
newsitem.headline: Nervous Danish bonds follow foreign markets down.

text.p: Danish bond prices opened lower and the Danish-German benchmark yield gap widened on Monday, with dealers seeing only a slight recovery likely.
"It's Friday's drop on Wall Street spreading to Europe and Denmark has caught it particularly badly," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 opened at 104.76, down 0.03 point from Friday's close, but by 0805 GMT had fallen further to 104.48. The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened to 96 basis points from Friday's 93 bp. The crown traded at 3.8637 per mark, weakening slightly from 3.8631. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969650
